Title: Randomized clinical trial comparing LigaSure haemorrhoidectomy with open diathermy haemorrhoidectomy
Author: Tan K.-Y.
Comment: No SDs, SEs, CIs or t-statistic reported for operative time; only group means and p<0.01. M_diff recorded as group_2_mean - group_1_mean = 18.2 - 9.4 = 8.8 min (diathermy minus LigaSure, i.e. LigaSure shorter by 8.8 min); p-value entered as the reported threshold 0.01 (actual p<0.01).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('LigaSure haemorrhoidectomy') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Participant type: Adults (19-71 years) with newly diagnosed symptomatic third and fourth degree haemorrhoids requiring haemorrhoidectomy
Recruitment source: Single centre, National Healthcare Group, Singapore (March-October 2007)
Outcome measurement: Duration of the haemorrhoidectomy procedure in minutes
effect_direction: favours LigaSure (9.4 vs 18.2 min; MD = -8.8 min)

Title: Haemorrhoidectomy: Randomised Controlled Clinical Trial of Ligasure Compared with Milligan-Morgan Operation
Author: Vara Thorbeck C, Felices Montes M
Comment: Operating time is reported as mean seconds PER HAEMORRHOIDAL CUSHION (total time divided by number of affected cushions), not total operation time in minutes; a fixed seconds-to-minutes conversion factor (1/60) is supplied, but the denominator remains 'per cushion' rather than 'per operation'. M_diff = group_2_mean - group_1_mean = 313 - 100 = 213 seconds (control minus Ligasure; i.e. Ligasure shorter), computed from the two explicitly reported means of a simple two-arm between-subjects design. p reported only as the threshold p < 0.01; no t value or df reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Ligasure system haemorrhoidectomy (variant of Milligan-Morgan, no pedicle ligation)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: patients with third and fourth degree symptomatic haemorrhoids (mean age 50 years; 66 men, 46 women)
Recruitment source: Teaching hospital (Hospital Clinico Universitario Virgen de la Victoria, Malaga), March 2000 - August 2001
Outcome measurement: Mean (SD) seconds per haemorrhoidal cushion, compared with Student's t test
effect_direction: favours LigaSure (100 s vs 313 s per cushion; shorter with LigaSure)

Title: Randomized clinical trial of LigaSure™ and conventional diathermy haemorrhoidectomy
Author: Muzi MG, Milito G, Nigro C, Cadeddu F, Andreoli F, Amabile D, Farinon AM
Comment: No SDs reported; dispersion given only as mean (range), so group_1_range_lower/upper and group_2_range_lower/upper hold the paper's reported RANGES around MEANS (not medians) — SD must be approximated downstream. M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean (20 − 11.5 = 8.5), i.e. diathermy minus LigaSure; under the review's convention (MD<0 favours LigaSure) this corresponds to MD = −8.5 min. The diathermy range (19.5–48) is asymmetric/implausible relative to its stated mean of 20, possibly a typographical error in the original table.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('LigaSure™ haemorrhoidectomy') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Participant type: adults with symptomatic grade III or IV haemorrhoids scheduled for day-case haemorrhoidectomy
Recruitment source: Day surgery unit, Department of Surgery, Tor Vergata University Hospital, Rome
Outcome measurement: Mean (range) operating time in minutes per arm, compared with Student's t test
effect_direction: favours LigaSure (11.5 vs 20 min; MD = -8.5 min)

Title: Clinical Experience of Sutureless Closed Hemorrhoidectomy with LigaSure™
Author: Chung & Wu
Comment: M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean (15.0 − 21.2 = −6.2) from explicitly reported means in a simple two-group between-subjects comparison. SE_diff derived from reported SDs and Ns using pooled SD: sp = 6.97, SE = 6.97*sqrt(1/31+1/30) = 1.78. df1 = n1+n2-2 = 59 (inferred, not reported). Abstract states P < 0.01 while Table 1 states P = 0.001.
Participant type: Patients with symptomatic Grade 3 or 4 hemorrhoids undergoing hemorrhoidectomy
Recruitment source: Consecutively operated patients, Surgical Department, Provincial Hsin-Chu Hospital, Taiwan (July–August 2001)
Outcome measurement: Mean ± standard deviation operating time in minutes per arm
effect_direction: favours LigaSure (15.0 vs 21.2 min; MD = -6.2 min)

Author: Milito G, Gargiani M, Cortese F

Title: Randomized Controlled Trial of LigaSure with Submucosal Dissection versus Ferguson Hemorrhoidectomy for Prolapsed Hemorrhoids
Author: Wang, Jaw-Yuan
Comment: Dispersion values are STANDARD ERRORS, not SDs (Methods: "Results were expressed as the mean – standard error"; Table 2 footnote "Mean – SE") and were recorded in the SE fields. M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean (34.2 − 11.3 = 22.9) from a simple two-arm between-subjects comparison; sign convention here is control minus treatment, i.e. LigaSure was 22.9 minutes shorter (MD = −22.9 in the plan's direction). Exact p value reported only as P < 0.0001; no t statistic or CI reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group 1: LigaSure hemorrhoidectomy with submucosal dissection') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); treatment SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n)); control SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n))
Participant type: Adults with symptomatic grade III or IV hemorrhoids
Recruitment source: Department of Surgery, Kaohsiung Medical University Hospital, consecutive patients November 2004 - April 2005
Outcome measurement: Mean operating time in minutes per arm, reported as mean ± standard error (Table 2 footnote: "Mean – SE")
effect_direction: favours LigaSure (11.3 vs 34.2 min; MD = -22.9 min)
